Before dispatching an agent, the worker checks:\n//! 1. **Concurrency limits**: Are fewer than `max_concurrent` workers using\n//!    this provider/model? ProviderConcurrencyExceeded {\n        provider: String,\n        current: u32,\n        limit: u32,\n    },\n    /// Model concurrency limit reached.\n    ModelConcurrencyExceeded {\n        model: RateLimitDecision::ProviderConcurrencyExceeded {\n                provider,\n                current,\n                limit,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"provider current,\n                limit,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"model '{}' concurrency exceeded ({}/{})\",\n                model, current, limit\n            ),\n            RateLimitDecision::RpmExceeded {\n                provider,\n                requests_per_minute,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"provider '{}' RPM limit let now = Utc::now();\n        let elapsed_secs = (now - self.last_refill).num_milliseconds().max(0) as f64 / 1000.0;\n        let refill_rate = self.capacity as f64 / 60.0; // tokens per second\n        self.tokens = (self.tokens + elapsed_secs * refill_rate).min(self.capacity as f64);\n        self.last_refill = now;\n    }\n\n    /// Try to consume one token. Returns true if successful.\n    fn try_consume(&mut self) -> bool {\n        self.refill();\n        if self.tokens >= 1.0 {\n            self.tokens -= 1.0;\n            true\n        } else {\n            false\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// RateLimiter\n//    }\n\n    /// Check all rate limits before dispatching.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Allowed` if dispatch can proceed, or a specific reason why not.\n    /// The caller should back off and retry if not allowed.\n    pub fn check(\n        &self,\n        provider: Option<&str>,\n        model: Option<&str>,\n        registry: &Registry,\n    ) -> Result<RateLimitDecision> {\n        // Check provider concurrency.\n        if let Some(provider_name) = provider {\n            if let Some(provider_limits) = self.config.providers.get(provider_name) {\n                if let             if !decision.is_allowed() {\n                        return Ok(decision);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Check model concurrency.\n           let decision =\n                        self.check_model_concurrency(model_name, max_concurrent, registry)?;\n                    if !decision.is_allowed() {\n                        return }\n\n    /// Check model concurrency against the worker registry.\n    fn check_model_concurrency(\n        &self,\n        model: &str,\n        max_concurrent: u32,\n        registry: &Registry,\n     .count() as u32;\n\n        if active_count >= max_concurrent {\n            Ok(RateLimitDecision::ModelConcurrencyExceeded {\n                model: model.to_string(),\n                current: std::fs::create_dir_all(&self.state_dir).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to create rate_limits directory: {}\",\n                self.state_dir.display()\n {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_a895ee3ed3b94b98815c5de3","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# NEEDLE Implementation Plan\n2\t\n3\t> **N**avigates **E**very **E**nqueued **D**eliverable, **L**ogs **E**ffort\n4\t\n5\t## Design Principles\n6\t\n7\tThese six principles are non-negotiable. Every design decision in this plan traces back to one or more of them.\n8\t\n9\t1. **Deterministic order.** Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same bead ordering. There is no randomness in selection. Ties are broken by creation time.\n10\t\n11\t2. **Explicit outcome paths.** Every possible result of every operation has a named handler. If an outcome can happen, it has a handler. If it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen. The type system enforces exhaustiveness.\n12\t\n13\t3. **Platform and model agnostic.** NEEDLE wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. It runs on any POSIX system. It does not depend on any specific AI provider, model, or API.\n14\t\n15\t4. **Observable by default.** Every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome emits structured telemetry. A silent worker is a broken worker. Telemetry is structured from origin (JSONL) and exportable as OpenTelemetry (OTLP) so any compliant backend — Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, FABRIC — can consume NEEDLE's signals without a custom adapter.\n16\t\n17\t5. **Self-healing.** Workers detect and recover from stuck states, stale claims, crashed peers, and corrupted databases without human intervention. Recovery paths are explicit, not heuristic.\n18\t\n19\t6. **Separation of concerns.** The orchestrator does not execute work. The agent does not manage state. The bead store does not enforce workflow. Each component has one job.\n20\t\n21\t---\n22\t\n23\t## Architecture Overview\n24\t\n25\tNEEDLE is composed of five layers:\n26\t\n27\t```\n28\t┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n29\t│                        CLI Layer                              │\n30\t│  needle run | stop | list | attach | status | config          │\n31\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n32\t│                     Worker Layer                              │\n33\t│  Worker loop, strand waterfall, session management            │\n34\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n35\t│                  Coordination Layer                            │\n36\t│  Claiming, locking, heartbeats, peer awareness                │\n37\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n38\t│                    Agent Layer                                 │\n39\t│  Adapter interface, dispatch, result capture                  │\n40\t├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n41\t│                   Foundation Layer                             │\n42\t│  Telemetry, configuration, bead store interface, self-healing │\n43\t└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n44\t```\n45\t\n46\t### Component Map\n47\t\n48\t| Component | Responsibility | Inputs | Outputs |\n49\t|-----------|---------------|--------|---------|\n50\t| **CLI** | Parse commands, manage sessions | User commands | Worker processes |\n51\t| **Worker** | Execute the strand waterfall loop | Bead queue state | Dispatch requests, state transitions |\n52\t| **StrandRunner** | Evaluate strands in sequence | Queue state, config | Next bead or escalation |\n53\t| **Claimer** | Atomic bead claiming with serialization | Candidate bead ID | Claimed bead or race-lost signal |\n54\t| **PromptBuilder** | Construct deterministic prompts from bead context | Claimed bead | Prompt string |\n55\t| **Dispatcher** | Load adapter, render template, execute agent | Prompt, adapter config | Agent process handle |\n56\t| **OutcomeHandler** | Route exit code to explicit handler | Exit code, stdout/stderr | State transition |\n57\t| **Telemetry** | Structured event emission | Any component event | JSONL records |\n58\t| **HealthMonitor** | Heartbeat, stuck detection, peer awareness | Worker state | Recovery actions |\n59\t| **ConfigLoader** | Hierarchical config resolution | Files, env, CLI args | Resolved config |\n60\t| **BeadStore** | Abstract interface to bead backend | CRUD operations | Bead records |\n61\t| **Mitosis** | Split multi-task beads into children with dedup | Failed bead, parent's existing children | Child beads or no-op |\n62\t\n63\t---\n64\t\n65\t## Language Decision\n66\t\n67\tThe implementation language must provide:\n68\t\n69\t| Requirement | Why | Source |\n70\t|-------------|-----|--------|\n71\t| Exhaustive pattern matching | Every outcome must be handled; compiler enforces it | Principle 2, bead-lifecycle-bugs.md |\n72\t| Real module system | 45K single-file bash was unmaintainable | bash-at-scale-problems.md |\n73\t| Structured error types | Silent failures caused cascading bugs | claim-race-conditions.md |\n74\t| Native JSON support | Fragile jq parsing corrupted state | worker-starvation-lessons.md |\n75\t| Proper concurrency primitives | flock/trap/PID files were inadequate | concurrency-approaches-compared.md |\n76\t| Single binary distribution | NEEDLE must be trivially installable | Principle 3 |\n77\t| Cross-platform | Linux, macOS at minimum | Principle 3 |\n78\t| Static analysis | Catch undefined functions, unused variables at compile time | bundler-build-integrity.md |\n79\t\n80\t**Recommended: Rust.** Exhaustive `match`, `Result<T, E>` error handling, `serde_json`, `tokio` for async, single binary via static linking, cross-compilation. The beads ecosystem already has Rust precedent (beads_rust, beads-polis).\n81\t\n82\t**Acceptable alternative: Go.** Simpler learning curve, good concurrency, single binary. Every design decision in this plan traces back to one or more of them.\n\n1. **Deterministic order.** Given the same queue state, every worker computes the same bead ordering. There is no randomness in selection. Ties are broken by creation time.\n\n2. **Explicit outcome paths.** Every possible result of every operation has a named handler. If an outcome can happen, it has a handler. If it doesn't have a handler, it cannot happen. The type system enforces exhaustiveness.\n\n3. **Platform and model agnostic.** NEEDLE wraps any headless CLI that accepts a prompt and exits. It runs on any POSIX system. It does not depend on any specific AI provider, model, or API.\n\n4. **Observable by default.** Every state transition, claim attempt, dispatch, and outcome emits structured telemetry. A silent worker is a broken worker. Telemetry is structured from origin (JSONL) and exportable as OpenTelemetry (OTLP) so any compliant backend — Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana, Honeycomb, Datadog, FABRIC — can consume NEEDLE's signals without a custom adapter.\n\n5. **Self-healing.** Workers detect and recover from stuck states, stale claims, crashed peers, and corrupted databases without human intervention. Recovery paths are explicit, not heuristic.\n\n6. **Separation of concerns.** The orchestrator does not execute work. The agent does not manage state. The bead store does not enforce workflow. Each component has one job.\n\n---\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\nNEEDLE is composed of five layers:\n\n```\n┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                        CLI Layer                              │\n│  needle run | stop | list | attach | status | config          │\n├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                     Worker Layer                              │\n│  Worker loop, strand waterfall, session management            │\n├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                  Coordination Layer                            │\n│  Claiming, locking, heartbeats, peer awareness                │\n├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                    Agent Layer                                 │\n│  Adapter interface, dispatch, result capture                  │\n├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                   Foundation Layer                             │\n│  Telemetry, configuration, bead store interface, self-healing │\n└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### Component Map\n\n| Component | Responsibility | Inputs | Outputs |\n|-----------|---------------|--------|---------|\n| **CLI** | Parse commands, manage sessions | User commands | Worker processes |\n| **Worker** | Execute the strand waterfall loop | Bead queue state | Dispatch requests, state transitions |\n| **StrandRunner** | Evaluate strands in sequence | Queue state, config | Next bead or escalation |\n| **Claimer** | Atomic bead claiming with serialization | Candidate bead ID | Claimed bead or race-lost signal |\n| **PromptBuilder** | Construct deterministic prompts from bead context | Claimed bead | Prompt string |\n| **Dispatcher** | Load adapter, render template, execute agent | Prompt, adapter config | Agent process handle |\n| **OutcomeHandler** | Route exit code to explicit handler | Exit code, stdout/stderr | State transition |\n| **Telemetry** | Structured event emission | Any component event | JSONL records |\n| **HealthMonitor** | Heartbeat, stuck detection, peer awareness | Worker state | Recovery actions |\n| **ConfigLoader** | Hierarchical config resolution | Files, env, CLI args | Resolved config |\n| **BeadStore** | Abstract interface to bead backend | {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_e61fc339a02646eaaca34c5f","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# ADR-008: Fleet Resource Safety — Enforced CPU/RAM Gating on Worker Launch\n2\t\n3\t**Status:** Proposed — 2026-07-21\n4\t**Deciders:** operator (jedarden), via Claude Code\n5\t**Tracking:** plan.md Phase 12\n6\t\n7\t## Context\n8\t\n9\tFound during a plan.md maturity review, cross-checking a previously-diagnosed operational incident against the current implementation. Plan.md already states the design intent (`docs/plan/plan.md:115`, `:1699-1718`): \"Fleet sizing is bounded by three runtime factors: provider inference throughput, available CPU, and available RAM. NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated.\" The implementation matches the word \"warns\" literally and does not go further.\n10\t\n11\t**What exists:** `RateLimiter::check_system_resources` (`src/rate_limit/mod.rs:350-400`) reads `/proc/loadavg` and `/proc/meminfo` and emits an `EventKind::FleetCpuSaturated` telemetry event plus a `tracing::warn!` when thresholds are crossed. Its return value is not consulted by any caller to gate or delay anything — it is a pure side-effecting observability call.\n12\t\n13\t**Where it's called:** only from `do_dispatch()` (`src/worker/mod.rs:1607-1612`) — inside an **already-running** worker's loop, immediately before executing a bead that worker has **already claimed**. It is never called during `worker_construction` (`src/cli/mod.rs:861-868`, a plain sequential `init_step(...)` call with no CPU/RAM gate before or during it), and never called during the `--count=N` sequential-launch sequence.\n14\t\n15\t**Launch spacing is a fixed interval, not load-adaptive:** `src/cli/mod.rs:637-638` — `if seq > 0 && stagger_secs > 0 { std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(stagger_secs)); }`, where `stagger_secs = config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds` defaults to `2` (`docs/plan/plan.md:1739`). This delay is the same whether the box is idle or already at 3x its core count in load average.\n16\t\n17\t**The gap this leaves, previously diagnosed operationally (2026-07-19, lab):** `worker_construction` is a genuinely slow (~5s) init step — it builds the agent adapter and warms the provider proxy connection. Under CPU saturation it can overrun whatever margin it has and the OS terminates the process before it completes — no Rust panic, no backtrace, just a worker that silently vanishes seconds after being launched. This was diagnosed by direct comparison: an identical launch command died twice at load ~2.5, then succeeded 90 minutes later at load ~0.74 with `worker_construction completed in 4992ms` — just under whatever margin exists. (The precise OS-level kill mechanism — cgroup pressure, systemd deadline, scheduler starvation past some other bound — was not re-diagnosed as part of this codebase review; what *is* newly confirmed by this review is that NEEDLE's own code has no gate that would prevent launching into this condition in the first place.) NEEDLE's own 60-second boot timeout (`src/cli/mod.rs:870-875`) cannot catch this class of failure, since it only evaluates *after* `init_step` returns — a process killed mid-step by something outside NEEDLE never reaches that check.\n18\t\n19\tNet effect: the one place in the codebase that actually reads system load (`check_system_resources`) is checked at the wrong point in the lifecycle to prevent the failure mode plan.md already anticipated in prose. It protects an already-running worker from starting *another* bead under saturation; it does nothing to stop a *new* worker from being launched into saturation in the first place, or to slow down a batch launch that is itself the cause of the saturation.\n20\t\n21\t## Decision\n22\t\n23\t1. **12.1 — Gate `worker_construction` on system resources, not just `do_dispatch`.** Before entering `worker_construction` (`src/cli/mod.rs`, around line 861), call `check_system_resources()` (or a renamed/generalized variant, since it's no longer rate-limit-specific once used here). If saturated (same thresholds already defined for `FleetCpuSaturated`), do not proceed into the slow construction step — retry with backoff (a few seconds, capped) until load drops below threshold or a max-wait is hit, at which point fail the launch with a clear, actionable error (`\"deferred N times, system still saturated (load X vs threshold Y) — launch aborted, retry when load drops\"`) rather than letting the OS silently kill an in-flight construction. This turns an unexplained vanished-worker into an explicit, loggable, retryable outcome.\n24\t2. **12.2 — Load-adaptive launch staggering.** Replace the fixed `launch_stagger_seconds` sleep in the `--count=N` sequential-launch path with a check against current load before each subsequent launch: if load is below a comfortable threshold, use the existing (short) default delay; if above it, extend the wait (bounded, with a cap) until load recedes or the cap is hit. This directly targets the failure mode where the *stagger itself* is what's supposed to prevent thundering-herd saturation but currently does so blindly regardless of whether the previous launches already pushed load past a safe point.\n25\t3. **12.3 — Apply the same gate to `needle supervise`'s auto-scale spawn path**, not only the CLI's `--count=N` path — the supervisor daemon (`src/supervisor/mod.rs`) is the other place new workers get launched, and it should not spawn a worker into saturation any more than a manual `--count=N` invocation should.\n26\t4. **Ship through the existing release path**: version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, staged canary rollout (`:testing` → `:stable`).\n27\t\n28\t## Consequences\n29\t\n30\t- Positive: closes the gap between plan.md's stated design intent (\"NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated\") and its actual behavior (monitors and warns only for an already-running worker's next-bead decision) — the fix is a matter of calling an existing function from two more call sites and consulting its result, not building new infrastructure.\n31\t- A deferred/retried launch under 12.1 changes `needle run`'s observable behavior under load — a launch that previously either silently died or (rarely) squeaked through now explicitly waits or explicitly fails with a reason. Plan.md already states the design intent (`docs/plan/plan.md:115`, `:1699-1718`): \"Fleet sizing is bounded by three runtime factors: provider inference throughput, available CPU, and available RAM. NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated.\" The implementation matches the word \"warns\" literally and does not go further.\n\n**What exists:** `RateLimiter::check_system_resources` (`src/rate_limit/mod.rs:350-400`) reads `/proc/loadavg` and `/proc/meminfo` and emits an `EventKind::FleetCpuSaturated` telemetry event plus a `tracing::warn!` when thresholds are crossed. Its return value is not consulted by any caller to gate or delay anything — it is a pure side-effecting observability call.\n\n**Where it's called:** only from `do_dispatch()` (`src/worker/mod.rs:1607-1612`) — inside an **already-running** worker's loop, immediately before executing a bead that worker has **already claimed**. It is never called during `worker_construction` (`src/cli/mod.rs:861-868`, a plain sequential `init_step(...)` call with no CPU/RAM gate before or during it), and never called during the `--count=N` sequential-launch sequence.\n\n**Launch spacing is a fixed interval, not load-adaptive:** `src/cli/mod.rs:637-638` — `if seq > 0 && stagger_secs > 0 { std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_secs(stagger_secs)); }`, where `stagger_secs = config.worker.launch_stagger_seconds` defaults to `2` (`docs/plan/plan.md:1739`). This delay is the same whether the box is idle or already at 3x its core count in load average.\n\n**The gap this leaves, previously diagnosed operationally (2026-07-19, lab):** `worker_construction` is a genuinely slow (~5s) init step — it builds the agent adapter and warms the provider proxy connection. Under CPU saturation it can overrun whatever margin it has and the OS terminates the process before it completes — no Rust panic, no backtrace, just a worker that silently vanishes seconds after being launched. This was diagnosed by direct comparison: an identical launch command died twice at load ~2.5, then succeeded 90 minutes later at load ~0.74 with `worker_construction completed in 4992ms` — just under whatever margin exists. (The precise OS-level kill mechanism — cgroup pressure, systemd deadline, scheduler starvation past some other bound — was not re-diagnosed as part of this codebase review; what *is* newly confirmed by this review is that NEEDLE's own code has no gate that would prevent launching into this condition in the first place.) NEEDLE's own 60-second boot timeout (`src/cli/mod.rs:870-875`) cannot catch this class of failure, since it only evaluates *after* `init_step` returns — a process killed mid-step by something outside NEEDLE never reaches that check.\n\nNet effect: the one place in the codebase that actually reads system load (`check_system_resources`) is checked at the wrong point in the lifecycle to prevent the failure mode plan.md already anticipated in prose. It protects an already-running worker from starting *another* bead under saturation; it does nothing to stop a *new* worker from being launched into saturation in the first place, or to slow down a batch launch that is itself the cause of the saturation.\n\n## Decision\n\n1. **12.1 — Gate `worker_construction` on system resources, not just `do_dispatch`.** Before entering `worker_construction` (`src/cli/mod.rs`, around line 861), call `check_system_resources()` (or a renamed/generalized variant, since it's no longer rate-limit-specific once used here). If saturated (same thresholds already defined for `FleetCpuSaturated`), do not proceed into the slow construction step — retry with backoff (a few seconds, capped) until load drops below threshold or a max-wait is hit, at which point fail the launch with a clear, actionable error (`\"deferred N times, system still saturated (load X vs threshold Y) — launch aborted, retry when load drops\"`) rather than letting the OS silently kill an in-flight construction. This turns an unexplained vanished-worker into an explicit, loggable, retryable outcome.\n2. **12.2 — Load-adaptive launch staggering.** Replace the fixed `launch_stagger_seconds` sleep in the `--count=N` sequential-launch path with a check against current load before each subsequent launch: if load is below a comfortable threshold, use the existing (short) default delay; if above it, extend the wait (bounded, with a cap) until load recedes or the cap is hit. This directly targets the failure mode where the *stagger itself* is what's supposed to prevent thundering-herd saturation but currently does so blindly regardless of whether the previous launches already pushed load past a safe point.\n3. **12.3 — Apply the same gate to `needle supervise`'s auto-scale spawn path**, not only the CLI's `--count=N` path — the supervisor daemon (`src/supervisor/mod.rs`) is the other place new workers get launched, and it should not spawn a worker into saturation any more than a manual `--count=N` invocation should.\n4. **Ship through the existing release path**: version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, staged canary rollout (`:testing` → `:stable`).\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Positive: closes the gap between plan.md's stated design intent (\"NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated\") and its actual behavior (monitors and warns only for an already-running worker's next-bead decision) — the fix is a matter of calling an existing function from two more call sites and consulting its result, not building new infrastructure.\n- A deferred/retried launch under 12.1 changes `needle run`'s observable behavior under load — a launch that previously either silently died or (rarely) squeaked through now explicitly waits or explicitly fails with a reason. Any external tooling (scripts, the fleet launcher wrapper) that assumes `needle run` returns immediately after backgrounding into tmux needs to tolerate a longer, bounded wait under saturation.\n- 12.2's adaptive stagger means a large `--count=N` batch launch on an already-busy host will take longer wall-clock time than before — this is the intended tradeoff (slower but reliable launches vs. fast but silently-lossy ones), consistent with the existing operational practice of manually staggering launches while watching `uptime`.\n- Does not address the separate, harder question of *how many workers is too many* for a given host long-term (that's the \"ready-bead supply is the real ceiling, not hardware\" finding from a separate operational audit) — this ADR is scoped to preventing a single launch from being silently killed mid-construction, not to fleet-sizing policy in general.\n\n## Evidence\n\n- `docs/plan/plan.md:115`, `:1699-1718` (stated design intent: \"NEEDLE monitors these and warns when saturated\").\n- `src/rate_limit/mod.rs:350-400` (`check_system_resources`, reads `/proc/loadavg`/`/proc/meminfo`, emits `FleetCpuSaturated`, return value unused by callers).\n- `src/worker/mod.rs:1607-1612` (only call site: `do_dispatch()`, already-running worker, already-claimed bead).\n- `src/cli/mod.rs:861-868` (`worker_construction` init step, no resource gate before/during); Driven by a previously-diagnosed operational incident (2026-07-19, lab): an identical `needle run` invocation died twice at load ~2.5 with no panic or backtrace (stderr ending mid-`worker_construction`), then succeeded 90 minutes later at load ~0.74 — load was the only variable that changed. Plan.md already states the design intent (\"NEEDLE monitors [CPU/RAM] and warns when saturated,\" `docs/plan/plan.md:115`); reviewing the implementation against that intent found the only resource check in the codebase (`check_system_resources`) is called exclusively from an already-running worker's dispatch loop, immediately before executing an already-claimed bead — never during `worker_construction` itself, and never during a `--count=N` batch launch, where the fixed (non-adaptive) launch stagger is the only thing standing between a batch launch and the saturation that kills its own later members. Full evidence and rationale in [ADR-008](../adr/008-fleet-resource-safety.md).\n\n## Changes\n\n### 12.1 Gate `worker_construction` on system resources\n- Before entering `worker_construction` (`src/cli/mod.rs`), call `check_system_resources()` (generalized beyond its current rate-limit-specific naming, since it's now used at launch time too). If saturated, retry with bounded backoff rather than proceeding into a step known to be slow (~5s) and vulnerable to being killed mid-step; if still saturated after the max wait, fail the launch with an explicit, actionable error instead of letting it vanish silently.\n\n### 12.2 Load-adaptive launch staggering\n- Replace the fixed `launch_stagger_seconds` sleep in the `--count=N` sequential-launch path (`src/cli/mod.rs`) with a load-aware delay: use the existing short default when load is comfortable, extend (bounded, capped) when it isn't, so a batch launch doesn't blindly push itself past the saturation threshold its own later members will then be killed by.\n\n### 12.3 Apply the same gate to `needle supervise`'s auto-scale path\n- `needle supervise` (`src/supervisor/mod.rs`) is the other place new workers get spawned (queue-depth-driven auto-scaling) — it should not spawn into saturation any more than a manual `--count=N` invocation should. Reuse 12.1's gate rather than a separate implementation.\n\n### 12.4 Testing\n- Regression test: `worker_construction` launched under a simulated saturated-load condition defers/retries instead of proceeding, and eventually fails with a named reason if saturation doesn't clear within the bound.\n- Regression test: a `--count=5` batch launch under simulated rising load produces increasing inter-launch delays, not a flat interval.\n- Regression test: `needle supervise`'s auto-scale spawn path respects the same gate as the CLI launch path (shared implementation, not divergent behavior).\n\n### 12.5 Deployment\n- Version bump, needle-ci (fmt + clippy + test on iad-ci), GitHub Release, staged canary rollout (`:testing` → `:stable`).\n\n## Exit criteria\n- No worker launch is silently killed mid-`worker_construction` under CPU saturation — the outcome is either a successful (possibly delayed) launch or an explicit, logged failure with a reason.\n- A `--count=N` batch launch on an already-loaded host does not itself push load high enough to kill its own later-launched members.\n- `needle supervise`'s auto-scaler and the CLI's manual launch path share one resource-gating implementation, not two that can drift apart.\n","numLines":30,"startLine":4317,"totalLines":4346}}}

Depends on: `config`, `registry`, `types`.\n\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\n\nuse anyhow::{Context, Result};\nuse chrono::{DateTime, Utc};\nuse fs2::FileExt;\nuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\n\nuse crate::config::LimitsConfig;\nuse crate::registry::Registry;\nuse crate::telemetry::{EventKind, Telemetry};\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// RateLimitDecision\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of a rate limit check.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]\npub enum RateLimitDecision {\n    /// Dispatch is allowed.\n    Allowed,\n    /// Provider concurrency limit reached.\n    ProviderConcurrencyExceeded {\n        provider: String,\n        current: u32,\n        limit: u32,\n    },\n    /// Model concurrency limit reached.\n    ModelConcurrencyExceeded {\n        model: String,\n        current: u32,\n        limit: u32,\n    },\n    /// RPM limit reached for this provider.\n    RpmExceeded {\n        provider: String,\n        requests_per_minute: u32,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl RateLimitDecision {\n    /// Whether dispatch is allowed.\n    pub fn is_allowed(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for RateLimitDecision {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            RateLimitDecision::Allowed => write!(f, \"allowed\"),\n            RateLimitDecision::ProviderConcurrencyExceeded {\n                provider,\n                current,\n                limit,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"provider '{}' concurrency exceeded ({}/{})\",\n                provider, current, limit\n            ),\n            RateLimitDecision::ModelConcurrencyExceeded {\n                model,\n                current,\n                limit,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"model '{}' concurrency exceeded ({}/{})\",\n                model, current, limit\n            ),\n            RateLimitDecision::RpmExceeded {\n                provider,\n                requests_per_minute,\n            } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"provider '{}' RPM limit exceeded ({}/min)\",\n                provider, requests_per_minute\n            ),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Token Bucket (file-based)\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// On-disk token bucket state for RPM limiting.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub struct TokenBucket {\n    /// Current available tokens (fractional for smooth refill).\n    pub tokens: f64,\n    /// Maximum tokens (= requests_per_minute).\n    pub capacity: u32,\n    /// Last time tokens were refilled.\n    pub last_refill: DateTime<Utc>,\n}\n\nimpl TokenBucket {\n    pub(crate) fn new(capacity: u32) -> Self {\n        TokenBucket {\n            tokens: capacity as f64,\n            capacity,\n            last_refill: Utc::now(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Refill tokens based on elapsed time since last refill.\n    fn refill(&mut self) {\n        let now = Utc::now();\n        let elapsed_secs = (now - self.last_refill).num_milliseconds().max(0) as f64 / 1000.0;\n        let refill_rate = self.capacity as f64 / 60.0; // tokens per second\n        self.tokens = (self.tokens + elapsed_secs * refill_rate).min(self.capacity as f64);\n        self.last_refill = now;\n    }\n\n    /// Try to consume one token. Returns true if successful.\n    fn try_consume(&mut self) -> bool {\n        self.refill();\n        if self.tokens >= 1.0 {\n            self.tokens -= 1.0;\n            true\n        } else {\n            false\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// RateLimiter\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Enforces provider/model concurrency limits and RPM rate limiting.\npub struct RateLimiter {\n    config: LimitsConfig,\n    /// Directory for token bucket state files (`~/.needle/state/rate_limits/`).\n    state_dir: PathBuf,\n}\n\nimpl RateLimiter {\n    /// Create a rate limiter with the given config and state directory.\n    pub fn new(config: LimitsConfig, state_dir: &Path) -> Self {\n        RateLimiter {\n            config,\n            state_dir: state_dir.join(\"rate_limits\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Check all rate limits before dispatching.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Allowed` if dispatch can proceed, or a specific reason why not.\n    /// The caller should back off and retry if not allowed.\n    pub fn check(\n        &self,\n        provider: Option<&str>,\n        model: Option<&str>,\n        registry: &Registry,\n    ) -> Result<RateLimitDecision> {\n        // Check provider concurrency.\n        if let Some(provider_name) = provider {\n            if let Some(provider_limits) = self.config.providers.get(provider_name) {\n                if let Some(max_concurrent) = provider_limits.max_concurrent {\n                    let decision =\n                        self.check_provider_concurrency(provider_name, max_concurrent, registry)?;\n                    if !decision.is_allowed() {\n                        return Ok(decision);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Check model concurrency.\n        if let Some(model_name) = model {\n            if let Some(model_limits) = self.config.models.get(model_name) {\n                if let Some(max_concurrent) = model_limits.max_concurrent {\n                    let decision =\n                        self.check_model_concurrency(model_name, max_concurrent, registry)?;\n                    if !decision.is_allowed() {\n                        return Ok(decision);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Check RPM.\n        if let Some(provider_name) = provider {\n            if let Some(provider_limits) = self.config.providers.get(provider_name) {\n                if let Some(rpm) = provider_limits.requests_per_minute {\n                    let decision = self.check_rpm(provider_name, rpm)?;\n                    if !decision.is_allowed() {\n                        return Ok(decision);\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        Ok(RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n    }\n\n    /// Check provider concurrency against the worker registry.\n    fn check_provider_concurrency(\n        &self,\n        provider: &str,\n        max_concurrent: u32,\n        registry: &Registry,\n    ) -> Result<RateLimitDecision> {\n        let workers = registry.list()?;\n        let active_count = workers\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|w| w.provider.as_deref() == Some(provider))\n            .count() as u32;\n\n        if active_count >= max_concurrent {\n            Ok(RateLimitDecision::ProviderConcurrencyExceeded {\n                provider: provider.to_string(),\n                current: active_count,\n                limit: max_concurrent,\n            })\n        } else {\n            Ok(RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Check model concurrency against the worker registry.\n    fn check_model_concurrency(\n        &self,\n        model: &str,\n        max_concurrent: u32,\n        registry: &Registry,\n    ) -> Result<RateLimitDecision> {\n        let workers = registry.list()?;\n        let active_count = workers\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|w| w.model.as_deref() == Some(model))\n            .count() as u32;\n\n        if active_count >= max_concurrent {\n            Ok(RateLimitDecision::ModelConcurrencyExceeded {\n                model: model.to_string(),\n                current: active_count,\n                limit: max_concurrent,\n            })\n        } else {\n            Ok(RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Check RPM via a file-based token bucket.\n    fn check_rpm(&self, provider: &str, rpm: u32) -> Result<RateLimitDecision> {\n        if rpm == 0 {\n            return Ok(RateLimitDecision::Allowed);\n        }\n\n        let allowed = self.try_acquire_rpm_token(provider, rpm)?;\n        if allowed {\n            Ok(RateLimitDecision::Allowed)\n        } else {\n            Ok(RateLimitDecision::RpmExceeded {\n                provider: provider.to_string(),\n                requests_per_minute: rpm,\n            })\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Try to acquire an RPM token from the file-based token bucket.\n    ///\n    /// Uses flock for cross-process safety.\n    fn try_acquire_rpm_token(&self, provider: &str, rpm: u32) -> Result<bool> {\n        // Ensure the rate_limits directory exists.\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(&self.state_dir).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to create rate_limits directory: {}\",\n                self.state_dir.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        let bucket_path = self.state_dir.join(format!(\"{provider}.json\"));\n\n        // Open or create the bucket file.\n        let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .read(true)\n            .write(true)\n            .create(true)\n            .truncate(false)\n            .open(&bucket_path)\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"failed to open rate limit bucket: {}\",\n                    bucket_path.display()\n                )\n            })?;\n\n        // Exclusive lock for atomic read-modify-write.\n        FileExt::lock_exclusive(&file).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to acquire lock on rate limit bucket: {}\",\n                bucket_path.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        // Read current state.\n        let content = std::fs::read_to_string(&bucket_path).unwrap_or_default();\n        let mut bucket: TokenBucket = if content.trim().is_empty() {\n            TokenBucket::new(rpm)\n        } else {\n            serde_json::from_str(&content).unwrap_or_else(|_| TokenBucket::new(rpm))\n        };\n\n        // Update capacity if config changed.\n        bucket.capacity = rpm;\n\n        // Try to consume a token.\n        let allowed = bucket.try_consume();\n\n        // Write updated state.\n        let json = serde_json::to_string_pretty(&bucket)\n            .context(\"failed to serialize token bucket state\")?;\n        std::fs::write(&bucket_path, &json).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to write rate limit bucket: {}\",\n                bucket_path.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        // Release lock.\n        FileExt::unlock(&file).with_context(|| {\n            format!(\n                \"failed to release lock on rate limit bucket: {}\",\n                bucket_path.display()\n            )\n        })?;\n\n        Ok(allowed)\n    }\n\n    /// Check system resource health (CPU load and memory).\n    ///\n    /// Emits structured telemetry events when thresholds are exceeded; does not\n    /// block dispatch. Logs tracing warnings in addition to telemetry for\n    /// operator visibility.\n    pub fn check_system_resources(\n        cpu_load_warn: f64,\n        memory_free_warn_mb: u64,\n        telemetry: &Telemetry,\n    ) {\n        // CPU load: read /proc/loadavg on Linux.\n        if let Ok(loadavg) = std::fs::read_to_string(\"/proc/loadavg\") {\n            if let Some(load_str) = loadavg.split_whitespace().next() {\n                if let Ok(load) = load_str.parse::<f64>() {\n                    // Normalize by number of CPUs.\n                    let num_cpus = std::thread::available_parallelism()\n                        .map(|n| n.get())\n                        .unwrap_or(1);\n                    let normalized = load / num_cpus as f64;\n                    if normalized > cpu_load_warn {\n                        tracing::warn!(\n                            load_1min = %load_str,\n                            normalized = %format!(\"{:.2}\", normalized),\n                            threshold = %format!(\"{:.2}\", cpu_load_warn),\n                            \"CPU load exceeds warning threshold\"\n                        );\n                        // Emit structured telemetry event.\n                        let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::FleetCpuSaturated {\n                            load_average: load,\n                            threshold: cpu_load_warn,\n                            core_count: num_cpus,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Memory: read /proc/meminfo on Linux.\n        if let Ok(meminfo) = std::fs::read_to_string(\"/proc/meminfo\") {\n            let mut mem_available_kb: Option<u64> = None;\n            for line in meminfo.lines() {\n                if line.starts_with(\"MemAvailable:\") {\n                    if let Some(val) = line.split_whitespace().nth(1) {\n                        mem_available_kb = val.parse().ok();\n                    }\n                    break;\n                }\n            }\n            if let Some(avail_kb) = mem_available_kb {\n                let avail_mb = avail_kb / 1024;\n                if avail_mb < memory_free_warn_mb {\n                    tracing::warn!(\n                        available_mb = avail_mb,\n                        threshold_mb = memory_free_warn_mb,\n                        \"available memory below warning threshold\"\n                    );\n                    // Emit structured telemetry event.\n                    let _ = telemetry.emit(EventKind::FleetMemoryLow {\n                        free_mb: avail_mb,\n                        threshold_mb: memory_free_warn_mb,\n                    });\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Tests\n// JSON value.\n    pub fn to_data(&self) -> serde_json::Value {\n        match self {\n            EventKind::WorkerBooting {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStarted {\n                worker_name,\n                version,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_name, \"version\": version })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerStopped {\n                reason,\n                beads_processed,\n                uptime_secs,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"reason\": reason,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                    \"uptime_secs\": uptime_secs,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerErrored {\n                error_type,\n                error_message,\n                beads_processed,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"error_type\": error_type,\n                    \"error_message\": error_message,\n                    \"beads_processed\": beads_processed,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerExhausted {\n                cycle_count,\n                last_strand,\n                waterfall_restarts,\n                restart_triggers,\n                strand_evaluations,\n            } => {\n                serde_json::json!({\n                    \"cycle_count\": cycle_count,\n                    \"last_strand_evaluated\": last_strand,\n                    \"waterfall_restarts\": waterfall_restarts,\n                    \"restart_triggers\": restart_triggers,\n                    \"strand_evaluations\": strand_evaluations,\n                })\n            }\n            EventKind::WorkerIdle { backoff_seconds } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"backoff_seconds\": backoff_seconds })\n            }\n            EventKind::StateTransition { from, to } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"from\": format!(\"{from}\"), \"to\": format!(\"{to}\") })\n            }\n            EventKind::InitStepStarted { step } => {\n                serde_json::json!({ \"step\": step ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Pluggable output backend for telemetry events.\n///\n/// Implement this trait to add a new sink — register an instance in the\n/// `TelemetryBus` and events fan out automatically, with no special-casing.\npub trait Sink: Send + Sync {\n    /// Accept a single event. Must not block indefinitely.\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Flush any buffered state before shutdown.\n    ///\n    /// Implementations should respect `deadline`: if flushing cannot complete\n    /// within the duration, return an error rather than blocking indefinitely.\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()>;\n}\n\n/// Blanket impl for Arc-wrapped sinks.\n/// This enables Arc<Sink> to be used wherever Sink is required.\nimpl<T: Sink + ?Sized> Sink for Arc<T> {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        self.as_ref().accept(event)\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        self.as_ref().flush(deadline)\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── FileSink ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Writes JSONL telemetry to `<log_dir>/<worker>-<session>.jsonl`.\n///\n/// Append-only, one line per event. The log directory is created if it\n/// does not exist.\npub struct FileSink {\n    path: PathBuf,\n    writer: std::sync::Mutex<std::io::BufWriter<std::fs::File>>,\n}\n\nimpl FileSink {\n    /// Construct a sink using the default log directory (`~/.needle/logs/`).\n    pub fn new(worker_id: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_else(|_| \".\".to_string());\n        let log_dir = PathBuf::from(&home).join(\".needle\").join(\"logs\");\n        Self::with_dir(&log_dir, worker_id, session_id)\n    }\n\n    /// Construct a sink writing to a specific directory.\n    ///\n    /// Creates the directory (and parents) if it does not exist.\n    pub fn with_dir(log_dir: &Path, worker_id: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<Self> {\n        std::fs::create_dir_all(log_dir)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to create log directory: {}\", log_dir.display()))?;\n        let filename = format!(\"{worker_id}-{session_id}.jsonl\");\n        let path = log_dir.join(filename);\n        let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n            .create(true)\n            .append(true)\n            .open(&path)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to open log file: {}\", path.display()))?;\n        Ok(FileSink {\n            path,\n            writer: std::sync::Mutex::new(std::io::BufWriter::new(file)),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Return the path to the log file.\n    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.path\n    }\n\n    /// Write a boot event directly to the file, bypassing the normal channel.\n    ///\n    /// This is called immediately after FileSink creation to ensure that even if\n    /// the writer thread fails to start, we have a trace in the JSONL file.\n    /// The event is written synchronously and flushed to disk.\n    fn write_boot_event_direct(\n        &self,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        session_id: &str,\n        version: &str,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        Self::write_boot_event_direct_impl(\n            &self.writer,\n            &self.path,\n            worker_id,\n            session_id,\n            version,\n            std::time::Duration::from_secs(5), // 5 second timeout\n        )\n    }\n\n    /// Write a boot event directly to the file with a timeout.\n    ///\n    /// This is a timeout-aware variant that prevents indefinite blocking on hung\n    /// filesystems (e.g., network filesystem issues, stale NFS mounts). If the\n    /// write takes longer than the timeout, it returns an error and the caller\n    /// can decide whether to continue or fail.\n    ///\n    /// The timeout is implemented by spawning a thread to do the blocking I/O\n    /// and joining with a timeout. If the timeout expires, the thread is detached\n    /// and will continue running (and eventually complete or be killed by the OS).\n    fn write_boot_event_direct_impl(\n        _writer: &std::sync::Mutex<std::io::BufWriter<std::fs::File>>,\n        path: &Path,\n        worker_id: &str,\n        session_id: &str,\n        version: &str,\n        timeout: std::time::Duration,\n    ) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        use std::sync::mpsc;\n        use std::thread;\n\n        let event = TelemetryEvent {\n            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n            event_type: \"worker.booting\".to_string(),\n            worker_id: worker_id.to_string(),\n            session_id: session_id.to_string(),\n            sequence: 0,\n            bead_id: None,\n            workspace: None,\n            duration_ms: None,\n            data: serde_json::json!({ \"worker_name\": worker_id, \"version\": version }),\n            trace_id: None,\n            span_id: None,\n        };\n        let line = serde_json::to_string(&event)?;\n        let path_for_error = path.display().to_string();\n        let path_clone = path.to_path_buf();\n\n        // JoinHandle::join() has no timeout in Rust's std — use a channel with recv_timeout.\n        let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel::<Result<(), String>>();\n\n        // The JoinHandle is intentionally dropped on timeout: dropping detaches the thread,\n        // which continues running until it completes or the process exits.\n        let _handle = thread::spawn(move || {\n            let result: Result<(), String> = (|| {\n                let file = std::fs::OpenOptions::new()\n                    .create(true)\n                    .append(true)\n                    .open(&path_clone)\n                    .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n                let mut writer = std::io::BufWriter::new(file);\n                writeln!(writer, \"{line}\").map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n                writer.flush().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n                writer.get_ref().sync_all().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n                Ok(())\n            })();\n            // Ignore send error: receiver may have timed out and been dropped.\n            let _ = tx.send(result);\n        });\n\n        match rx.recv_timeout(timeout) {\n            Ok(Ok(())) => Ok(()),\n            Ok(Err(e)) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n                \"failed to write boot event to {}: {}\",\n                path_for_error,\n                e\n            )),\n            Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Timeout) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n                \"timed out writing boot event to {} after {:?} (filesystem may be hung)\",\n                path_for_error,\n                timeout\n            )),\n            Err(mpsc::RecvTimeoutError::Disconnected) => Err(anyhow::anyhow!(\n                \"boot event writer thread disconnected for {}\",\n                path_for_error\n            )),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for FileSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        let line = serde_json::to_string(event)?;\n        let mut writer = self\n            .writer\n            .lock()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"lock poisoned: {}\", e))?;\n        writeln!(writer, \"{line}\")?;\n        writer.flush()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, _deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        let mut writer = self\n            .writer\n            .lock()\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"lock poisoned: {}\", e))?;\n        writer.flush()?;\n        // fsync to ensure durability before shutdown\n        writer.get_ref().sync_all()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── StdoutSink ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Human-readable, color-coded telemetry sink for interactive monitoring.\n///\n/// Format: `HH:MM:SS [worker] EVENT detail`\npub struct StdoutSink {\n    format: StdoutFormat,\n    use_color: bool,\n}\n\nimpl StdoutSink {\n    /// Create a new stdout sink from config.\n    pub fn new(config: &StdoutSinkConfig) -> Self {\n        let use_color = match config.color {\n            ColorMode::Always => true,\n            ColorMode::Never => false,\n            ColorMode::Auto => atty_stdout(),\n        };\n        StdoutSink {\n            format: config.format,\n            use_color,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Format a single event as a human-readable line.\n    pub fn format_event(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> String {\n        let time = event.timestamp.format(\"%H:%M:%S\");\n        let worker = &event.worker_id;\n        let etype = &event.event_type;\n\n        // Build the summary portion based on event type.\n        let summary = self.event_summary(event);\n\n        match self.format {\n            StdoutFormat::Minimal => {\n                let line = format!(\"{time} [{worker}] {etype}\");\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n            StdoutFormat::Normal => {\n                let bead_part = event\n                    .bead_id\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map(|b| format!(\" {}\", b.as_ref()))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let summary_part = if summary.is_empty() {\n                    String::new()\n                } else {\n                    format!(\" ({summary})\")\n                };\n                let line = format!(\n                    \"{time} [{worker}] {}{bead_part}{summary_part}\",\n                    Self::short_type(etype)\n                );\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n            StdoutFormat::Verbose => {\n                let bead_part = event\n                    .bead_id\n                    .as_ref()\n                    .map(|b| format!(\" {}\", b.as_ref()))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let data_part = if event.data.is_object()\n                    && event.data.as_object().map_or(true, |m| m.is_empty())\n                {\n                    String::new()\n                } else {\n                    format!(\" {}\", event.data)\n                };\n                let dur = event\n                    .duration_ms\n                    .map(|d| format!(\" {}ms\", d))\n                    .unwrap_or_default();\n                let line = format!(\n                    \"{time} [{worker}] {}{bead_part}{dur}{data_part}\",\n                    Self::short_type(etype)\n                );\n                if self.use_color {\n                    self.colorize(etype, &line)\n                } else {\n                    line\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Shorten the dotted event type to an uppercase action word.\n    fn short_type(event_type: &str) -> &str {\n        match event_type {\n            \"worker.started\" => \"STARTED\",\n            \"worker.stopped\" => \"STOPPED\",\n            \"worker.errored\" => \"ERROR\",\n            \"worker.exhausted\" => \"EXHAUSTED\",\n            \"worker.idle\" => \"IDLE\",\n            \"worker.state_transition\" => \"STATE\",\n            \"worker.queue_empty\" => \"QUEUE_EMPTY\",\n            \"strand.evaluated\" => \"STRAND\",\n            \"strand.skipped\" => \"STRAND_SKIP\",\n            \"bead.claim.attempted\" => \"CLAIMING\",\n            \"bead.claim.succeeded\" => \"CLAIMED\",\n            \"bead.claim.race_lost\" => \"RACE_LOST\",\n            \"bead.claim.race_lost_skipped\" => \"RACE_LOST_SKIP\",\n            \"bead.claim.failed\" => \"CLAIM_FAIL\",\n            \"bead.released\" => \"RELEASED\",\n            \"bead.completed\" => \"COMPLETED\",\n            \"bead.orphaned\" => \"ORPHANED\",\n            \"agent.dispatched\" => \"DISPATCHED\",\n            \"agent.completed\" => \"AGENT_DONE\",\n            \"outcome.classified\" => \"OUTCOME\",\n            \"outcome.handled\" => \"HANDLED\",\n            \"heartbeat.emitted\" => \"HEARTBEAT\",\n            \"peer.stale\" => \"PEER_STALE\",\n            \"peer.crashed\" => \"PEER_CRASHED\",\n            \"health.check\" => \"HEALTH\",\n            \"effort.recorded\" => \"EFFORT\",\n            \"budget.warning\" => \"BUDGET_WARN\",\n            \"budget.stop\" => \"BUDGET_STOP\",\n            \"rate_limit.wait\" => \"RATE_WAIT\",\n            \"rate_limit.allowed\" => \"RATE_OK\",\n            \"bead.mitosis.evaluated\" => \"MITOSIS_EVAL\",\n            \"bead.mitosis.split\" => \"MITOSIS\",\n            \"bead.mitosis.skipped\" => \"MITOSIS_SKIP\",\n            \"mend.orphaned_lock_removed\" => \"MEND_LOCK\",\n            \"mend.dependency_cleaned\" => \"MEND_DEP\",\n            \"mend.db_repaired\" => \"MEND_REPAIR\",\n            \"mend.db_rebuilt\" => \"MEND_REBUILD\",\n            \"mend.cycle_summary\" => \"MEND_DONE\",\n            \"telemetry.sink_error\" => \"SINK_ERR\",\n            other => other,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Produce a brief summary from the event data.\n    fn event_summary(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> String {\n        let d = &event.data;\n        match event.event_type.as_str() {\n            \"bead.claim.succeeded\" => String::new(),\n            \"agent.dispatched\" => d[\"agent\"]\n                .as_str()\n                .map(|a| format!(\"agent={a}\"))\n                .unwrap_or_default(),\n            \"agent.completed\" => {\n                let exit = d[\"exit_code\"].as_i64().unwrap_or(-1);\n                let dur = d[\"duration_ms\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"exit={exit}, {}\", format_duration_ms(dur))\n            }\n            \"outcome.classified\" => d[\"outcome\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string(),\n            \"outcome.handled\" => {\n                let outcome = d[\"outcome\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                let action = d[\"action\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                format!(\"{outcome} → {action}\")\n            }\n            \"effort.recorded\" => {\n                let agent = d[\"agent_name\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                let cost = d[\"estimated_cost_usd\"].as_f64();\n                let dur = d[\"elapsed_ms\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                match cost {\n                    Some(c) => format!(\"{agent}, {}, ${c:.4}\", format_duration_ms(dur)),\n                    None => format!(\"{agent}, {}\", format_duration_ms(dur)),\n                }\n            }\n            \"worker.stopped\" => {\n                let reason = d[\"reason\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"?\");\n                let beads = d[\"beads_processed\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"{reason}, {beads} beads\")\n            }\n            \"worker.errored\" => d[\"error_message\"].as_str().unwrap_or(\"unknown\").to_string(),\n            \"worker.idle\" => {\n                let secs = d[\"backoff_seconds\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"backoff {secs}s\")\n            }\n            \"bead.mitosis.split\" => {\n                let created = d[\"children_created\"].as_u64().unwrap_or(0);\n                format!(\"{created} children\")\n            }\n            \"budget.warning\" | \"budget.stop\" => {\n                let cost = => String::new(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Wrap text in ANSI color based on event type category.\n    fn colorize(&self, event_type: &str, text: &str) -> String {\n        let code = match event_type {\n            t if t.starts_with(\"worker.errored\") || t.starts_with(\"budget.stop\") => \"\\x1b[31m\", // red\n            t if t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.succeeded\") || t == \"bead.completed\" => \"\\x1b[32m\", // green\n            t if t.starts_with(\"agent.\") || t.starts_with(\"outcome.\") => \"\\x1b[36m\", // cyan\n            t if t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.race_lost\")\n                || t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.race_lost_skipped\")\n                || t.starts_with(\"bead.claim.failed\")\n                || t == \"bead.released\"\n                || t == \"bead.orphaned\" =>\n            {\n                \"\\x1b[33m\"\n            } // yellow\n            t if t.starts_with(\"budget.warning\") || t.starts_with(\"rate_limit\") => \"\\x1b[33m\", // yellow\n            t if t.starts_with(\"mend.\") || t.starts_with(\"peer.\") => \"\\x1b[35m\", // magenta\n            t if t.starts_with(\"heartbeat\") || t.starts_with(\"health\") => \"\\x1b[90m\", // dim\n            _ => \"\\x1b[0m\",                                                      // reset / default\n        };\n        format!(\"{code}{text}\\x1b[0m\")\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for StdoutSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        let line = self.format_event(event);\n        println!(\"{line}\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, _deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        std::io::stdout().flush()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n/// Check if stdout is a terminal (for auto color detection).\nfn atty_stdout() -> bool {\n    unsafe { libc_isatty(1) != 0 }\n}\n\nextern \"C\" {\n    #[link_name = \"isatty\"]\n    fn {\n        format!(\"{:.1}s\", ms as f64 / 1000.0)\n    } else {\n        let mins = ms / 60_000;\n        let secs = (ms % 60_000) / 1000;\n        format!(\"{mins}m{secs}s\")\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Session ID generation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Generate an 8-hex-char session ID.\n///\n/// Uses `/dev/urandom` when available, falls back to PID XOR timestamp.\npub fn generate_session_id() -> String {\n    // Try /dev/urandom (Linux/macOS)\n    if let Ok(mut f) = std::fs::File::open(\"/dev/urandom\") {\n        use std::io::Read;\n        let mut buf = [0u8; 4];\n        if f.read_exact(&mut buf).is_ok() {\n            return format!(\"{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}{:02x}\", buf[0], buf[1], buf[2], buf[3]);\n        }\n    }\n    // Fallback: PID XOR nanosecond timestamp\n    let pid = std::process::id();\n    let ts = Utc::now().timestamp_millis() as u64;\n    let hash = pid as u64 ^ ts;\n    format!(\"{:08x}\", hash & 0xffff_ffff)\n}\n\n// ─── Trace context helpers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Returns `(trace_id_hex, span_id_hex)` from the current OTel span context,\n/// or `(None, None)` when not inside a valid span.\n#[cfg(feature = \"otlp\")]\nfn current_trace_ids() -> (Option<String>, Option<String>) {\n    use opentelemetry::trace::TraceContextExt;\n    let ctx = opentelemetry::Context::current();\n    let binding = ctx.span();\n    let span_ctx = binding.span_context();\n    if span_ctx.is_valid() {\n        (\n            Some(hex::encode(span_ctx.trace_id().to_bytes())),\n Option<String>) {\n    (None, None)\n}\n\n// ─── HookSink ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A compiled hook: a pre-compiled regex filter + dispatch target(s).\nstruct CompiledHook {\n    filter: regex::Regex,\n    /// Shell command (empty = disabled).\n    command: String,\n    /// Webhook URL (None = disabled).\n    url: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// Dispatches matching telemetry events to external commands and/or URLs.\n///\n/// Each hook has a glob pattern matched against `event_type`. When an event\n/// matches, the event JSON is piped to `command`'s stdin and/or HTTP-POSTed\n/// to `url`. Execution is fire-and-forget — failed hooks emit `SinkError`\n/// events to the file sink but never block the worker or recurse into hooks.\npub struct HookSink {\n    hooks: Vec<CompiledHook>,\n}\n\nimpl HookSink {\n    /// Compile hook configs into a `HookSink`.\n    ///\n    /// Returns an error if any `event_filter` is an invalid glob pattern.\n    pub fn new(configs: &[crate::config::HookConfig]) -> Result<Self> {\n        let mut hooks = Vec::with_capacity(configs.len());\n        for cfg in configs {\n            let filter = glob_to_regex(&cfg.event_filter)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"invalid hook filter: {}\", cfg.event_filter))?;\n            hooks.push(CompiledHook {\n                filter,\n                command: cfg.command.clone(),\n                url: cfg.url.clone(),\n            });\n        }\n        Ok(HookSink { hooks })\n    }\n\n    /// Check whether any hooks are configured.\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.hooks.is_empty()\n    }\n\n    /// Dispatch an event to all matching hooks (fire-and-forget).\n    ///\n    /// Returns a list of `SinkError` events for hooks that failed, so the\n    /// caller can write them to the file sink without recursion.\n    pub fn dispatch(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Vec<TelemetryEvent> {\n        // Never dispatch SinkError events to hooks — prevents recursion.\n        if event.event_type == \"telemetry.sink_error\" {\n            return Vec::new();\n        }\n\n        let json = match serde_json::to_string(event) {\n            Ok(j) => j,\n            Err(_) => return Vec::new(),\n        };\n\n        let mut failures = Vec::new();\n        for hook in &self.hooks {\n            if !hook.filter.is_match(&event.event_type) {\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Dispatch to command if configured.\n            if !hook.command.is_empty() {\n                match Self::run_hook(&hook.command, &json) {\n                    Ok(()) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        failures.push(TelemetryEvent {\n                            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n                            event_type: \"telemetry.sink_error\".to_string(),\n                            worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                            session_id: event.session_id.clone(),\n                            sequence: 0, // sequence is set by the emitter, not here\n                            bead_id: None,\n                            workspace: None,\n                            data: serde_json::json!({\n                                \"hook_command\": hook.command,\n                                \"event_filter\": hook.filter.as_str(),\n                                \"original_event_type\": event.event_type,\n                                \"error\": e.to_string(),\n                            }),\n                            duration_ms: None,\n                            trace_id: None,\n                            span_id: None,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n\n            // Dispatch to URL if configured.\n            if let Some(ref url) = hook.url {\n                match Self::post_url(url, &json) {\n                    Ok(()) => {}\n                    Err(e) => {\n                        failures.push(TelemetryEvent {\n                            timestamp: Utc::now(),\n                            event_type: \"telemetry.sink_error\".to_string(),\n                            worker_id: event.worker_id.clone(),\n                            session_id: event.session_id.clone(),\n                            sequence: 0,\n                            bead_id: None,\n                            workspace: None,\n                            data: serde_json::json!({\n                                \"hook_url\": url,\n                                \"event_filter\": hook.filter.as_str(),\n                                \"original_event_type\": event.event_type,\n                                \"error\": e.to_string(),\n                            }),\n                            duration_ms: None,\n                            trace_id: None,\n                            span_id: None,\n                        });\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        failures\n    }\n\n    /// Execute a single hook command, piping JSON to its stdin.\n    ///\n    /// Spawns `sh -c <command>` with the event JSON on stdin, waits for\n    /// completion, and returns an error if the command exits non-zero.\n    /// This runs inside the background writer task so blocking is acceptable.\n    fn run_hook(command: &str, json: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        use std::io::Write;\n        use std::process::{Command, Stdio};\n\n        let mut child = Command::new(\"sh\")\n            .arg(\"-c\")\n            .arg(command)\n            .stdin(Stdio::piped())\n            .stdout(Stdio::null())\n            .stderr(Stdio::null())\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn hook: {command}\"))?;\n\n        if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {\n            // Best-effort write; ignore broken pipe if child exits early.\n            let _ = stdin.write_all(json.as_bytes());\n        }\n\n        // Wait for the child and check exit status.\n        let status = child\n            .wait()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to wait for hook: {command}\"))?;\n\n        if !status.success() {\n            anyhow::bail!(\n                \"hook exited with status {}: {command}\",\n                status.code().unwrap_or(-1)\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// HTTP POST the event JSON to a webhook URL.\n    ///\n    /// Sets `Content-Type: application/json` and applies a 10-second timeout.\n    /// Returns an error if the request fails or the This runs inside the background writer task so blocking is\n    /// acceptable.\n    fn post_url(url: &str, json: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        ureq::post(url)\n            .set(\"Content-Type\", \"application/json\")\n            .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(10))\n            .send_string(json)\n            .map_err(|e| anyhow::anyhow!(\"webhook POST to {url} failed: {e}\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Sink for HookSink {\n    fn accept(&self, event: &TelemetryEvent) -> Result<()> {\n        let failures = self.dispatch(event);\n        for fail in &failures {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                hook_error = %fail.data,\n                original_event = %event.event_type,\n                \"telemetry hook dispatch failed\"\n            );\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    fn flush(&self, _deadline: std::time::Duration) -> Result<()> {\n        // hooks run synchronously in accept(); nothing to drain\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Telemetry emitter ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Non-blocking telemetry emitter.\n///\n/// Cloning a `Telemetry` handle is cheap — it shares the same background\n/// writer and sequence counter.\n///\n/// The writer task must be started by calling `start()` from within a tokio\n/// runtime context.
